body.translated_text:
Composed by <s>Paṇḍitāśoka</s>
<s>Sāmānyadūṣaṇadikprasāritā</s> (Extension of the Refutation of Universals)

children.translated_text: By those who have postulated a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) that is all-pervading, eternal, and one,
for the cutting of their knot of delusion, its non-existence is here established.

body.text: kathamidamavagamyate / parasparavilakṣaṇakṣaṇeṣu pratyakṣasamīkṣyamāṇeṣvabhinnadhīdhvaniprasavanibandhanamanuyāyirūpaṃ sāmānyaṃ na mānyaṃ mānīṣiṇāmiti / sādhakapramāṇavirahāt bādhakapramāṇasambhavācceti brūmaḥ / tathāhi yadidaṃ sāmānyasādhanamanumānamabhidhīyate paraiḥ / yadanugatākāraṃ jñānaṃ tadanugatavastunibandhanaṃ yathā bahuṣu puṣpeṣu srak sragiti jñānaṃ / asti ca parasparasamparkavikalakalāsu kāryyādivyaktiṣvanugatākāraṃ vijñānaṃ tadanaikāntikatādoṣākrāntaśarīratvānna tadbhāvasādhanāyālaṃ / yato bhavati bahuṣu pācakeṣu pācakaḥ pācaka iti ekākāraparāmarśapratyayaḥ / na ca teṣvanugatamekaṃ vastu samasti / tadbhāve hi prāgeva tathāvidhapratyayotpādaprasaṅgo durvvārapracāraḥ / kriyopakārāpekṣāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇānāṃ sāmānyavyañjakatvādayamadoṣa iti cet / naitadasti / nityānāmanādheyātiśayatayānupakāriṇi sahakāriṇyapekṣāyogāt / sātiśayatve vā pratikṣaṇaṃ viśarārūśarīratvāt kriyā kuta iti doṣoduṣpariharaḥ / kriyānibandhanatvāt pācakeṣvanugatākārapratyayasya nānaikāntikatādoṣa ityapi vārttaṃ / pratibhedaṃ bhidyamānānāṃ karmmaṇāṃ tannibandhanatvāyogāt / bhinnānāmapyabhinnākārajñānanibandhanatve vyaktīnāmapi tathā bhāvo na rāja daṇḍanivāritaḥ / tataśca sāmānyameva nopeyaṃ syāt / iti mūlaharaṃ pakṣamāśrayatā devānāṃ priyeṇa suṣṭha anukūlamācaritaṃ / anenaiva nyāyena kriyākārakasambandhamabhinnajñānanibandhanamupakalpayan pratikṣiptaḥ / pākakriyātvanibandhanaḥ pācakeṣvanugatākāraḥ pratyayastato nānaikāntikatādoṣa ityapi na mantavyaṃ / nahyarthāntarasambandhinī jātirarthāntarapratyayotpattihetuḥ, atiprasaṅgāt / syādetat samavetasamavāyasambandhabalāt pākakriyāsāmānyaṃ pācakeṣvabhinnākāraṃ parāmarśapratyayamupajanayati tato na yathoktadoṣaḥ / tadidamapyasāraṃ / yat udayānantarāpavarjjitayā karmmaṇāmevāsambhavāt, vinaṣṭe karmmaṇi tat sāmānyaṃ na karmmaṇi tadabhāvādeva nāpi karttarīti sambadvasambandhopyasya nāstīti nābhinnapratyayahetuḥ / tasmāt sthitametattadanaikāntikatādoṣaduṣṭatvānnedamanumānaṃ sāmānyasattvāsādhanāya paryyāptamiti / itaścāpi na sāmānyasattvāsādhanamidamanumānaṃ / yathaiva hi parasparāsaṅkīrṇasvabhāvā api śābaleyādayobhāvāḥ kayācideva tadekakāryyapratiniyamalakṣaṇayā svahetubalāyātayā prakṛtyā tadekamabhimatamanugatarūpamupakurbbate, tadaparasāmānyāntaramantareṇānyathānavasthāprasaṅgāt / tathā tamekaṃ parāmarśapratyayamupajanayantu kimantarālagaḍunā vyatirekavatā sāmānyenopagatena /
body.translated_text: How is this understood? We say: among mutually distinct momentary things perceived directly, the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal)—a continuous form that is the ground for the production of cognitions and words of non-difference—is not to be esteemed by the wise, because of the absence of a validating <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) and because of the possibility of a refuting <s>pramāṇa</s>. For consider: this inference for establishing the universal stated by the opponents—'Whatever cognition has a common form, that has a common object as its ground, just as the cognition "garland, garland" regarding many flowers'—and there is cognition with a common form regarding individual instances of effects and the like that are devoid of mutual contact—since this [inference] has a body vitiated by the fault of <s>anaikāntikatā</s> (inconclusiveness), it is not sufficient to establish the existence of that [universal]. For there arises regarding many cooks the apprehending cognition of one form 'cook, cook,' but among them there is no single common object. For if such [a universal] existed, there would be the undesirable consequence that such cognition would arise even before [the present moment], an unstoppable progression. If [you say] this is not a fault because the <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars), which depend on the assistance of action, are manifesters of the universal—this is not so, because for permanent entities, since no excellence can be superimposed upon them, there is no possibility of depending on cooperating conditions that do not assist them. Or if there were excellence [in the universal], then the objection—'Whence comes action, since [the universal] would at every moment have a different body?'—is difficult to refute. The claim that there is no fault of inconclusiveness for the cognition of common form regarding cooks because it is grounded in action—this too is unacceptable, because actions, which differ in each instance, cannot serve as the ground for that [common cognition]. If things that are different can be the ground for cognition of identical form, then the same status for individual instances [without a universal] is not prevented by royal decree. And therefore the universal itself would not need to be accepted. Thus by the 'friend of the gods' [the opponent], in resorting to this root-destroying position, most agreeable work has been done! By this very reasoning, the one who proposes the relation of action and agent as the ground for cognition of identity is refuted. Nor should one think that the cognition of common form among cooks, grounded in the nature of cooking action, is therefore free from the fault of inconclusiveness. For a <s>jāti</s> (genus) belonging to one entity is not the cause of the arising of cognition regarding another entity, because of over-extension. It may be objected that by the force of the relation of <s>samavetasamavāya</s> (inherence-in-what-inheres), the universal of cooking action produces a cognition of apprehension of identical form regarding cooks, and therefore the stated fault does not apply. But this too is without substance. Because of the impossibility of actions existing apart from their immediately subsequent moment of arising, when the action has perished, that universal is not in the action—since it does not exist—nor in the agent; therefore it has no connected relation, and thus it is not the cause of the cognition of identity. Therefore it is established that this inference, being vitiated by the fault of inconclusiveness, is not sufficient for establishing the existence of the universal. And for the following reason too, this inference does not establish the existence of the universal: just as entities such as piebald cows and the like, though having mutually unmixed natures, by some inherent nature arising from the force of their own causes, characterized by being restricted to that one effect, contribute to that one agreed-upon common form—since otherwise there would be the fallacy of infinite regress without positing yet another intervening universal—so let them produce that one apprehending cognition in the same way. What need is there for an intervening useless universal endowed with distinctness?

body.text: athocyate pratiniyataśaktayaḥ sarvvabhāvāḥ / etacca sāmānyāpalāpibhirapi niyatamabhyupagamanīyaṃ anyathā kutaḥ śālivījaṃ śālyaṅkurameva janayati na kodravāṅkuramiti / paraparyyanuyoge bhāvaprakṛtiṃ muktvā kimaparamiha vacanīyamasti / etaccottaramasmākamapi na vanaukaḥkulakavalitaṃ, tathāhi vayamapyevaṃ śaktā eva vaktuṃ sāmānyamevopakarttuṃ śaktivyaktīnāṃ bhedāviśeṣe 'pi na tadekaṃ vijñānamupajanayitumiti / anuttaraṃ vata doṣasaṅkaṭamatrabhavān dṛṣṭidoṣeṇa praviśyamāno 'pi nātmānamātmanā sambedayate / tathāhi śālivījatadaṅkurayoradhyakṣānupalambhanibandhane kāryyakāraṇabhāve 'vagate śālivījaṃ śālyaṅkuraṃ janayituṃ śaktaṃ na kodravāṅkuramiti śakyamabhidhātuṃ / naivaṃ sāmānyatadvatorupakāryyopakārakabhāvaḥ kutaścana pramāṇānniścitaḥ / tatkathamidamuttaramabhidhīyamānamādadhīta sādhimānamityalamalīkanirbandhanena / na sādhakapramāṇavirahamātreṇa prekṣāvatāmasadvyavahāraḥ / tatastadabhāvasādhakamanumānamabhidhīyamānamasmābhirākalyatāṃ / yadyadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sannopalabhyate tattadasaditi prekṣāvadbhirvyavaharttavyaṃ, yathāmbarāmburuhaṃ, nopalabhyate copalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sāmānyaṃ kvacidapīti svabhāvānupalabdhiḥ / na cātrāsidvidoṣodbhāvanayā pratyavasthātavyam / tathā hyatrāsidvirbhavantī svarūpato viśeṣaṇato vā bhavet / tatra na tāvadādyaṃ sambhavati / anyopalambharupasyānupalambhasyābhyupagamāt / tasya ca svasambedanapratyakṣasākṣātkṛtasvarūpatvāt kutaḥ svarūpāsidvadoṣāvakāśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now it is said: all entities have specific capacities (<s>pratiniyataśaktayaḥ sarvabhāvāḥ</s>). And this must necessarily be accepted even by those who deny universals (<s>sāmānya</s>). Otherwise, why does a rice seed produce only a rice sprout and not a <s>kodrava</s> (millet) sprout? In response to this counter-objection, what else is there to say beyond the nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of entities? And this reply of ours is not one that has been devoured by a pack of forest-dwellers [i.e., easily defeated]. For we too are able to say thus: even if the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) alone assists, despite there being no difference among the manifestations of capacity, it cannot generate a single cognition. Alas, what an inescapable tangle of faults! This worthy one, even while entering into it through a defect of vision, does not recognize himself by himself. For when the cause-effect relationship between the rice seed and its sprout is understood to be grounded in the non-apprehension by direct perception, it can be stated that the rice seed is capable of producing a rice sprout and not a <s>kodrava</s> sprout. But the relationship of beneficiary and benefactor between the universal and its instances is not established by any means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Therefore, how can this reply, when stated, bear any authority? Enough with insistence on falsehood! The mere absence of an establishing means of valid cognition does not lead the discerning to treat something as non-existent. Therefore, let the inference (<s>anumāna</s>) establishing its non-existence, as stated by us, be heard: whatever, while fulfilling the conditions of apprehensibility (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), is nonetheless not apprehended, that should be treated as non-existent by the discerning — like a sky-lotus. And the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), though fulfilling the conditions of apprehensibility, is not apprehended anywhere — this is the non-apprehension of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>). Nor should one resist here by raising the fault of unestablishedness (<s>asiddhi</s>). For the unestablishedness here would be either of the intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) or of the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>). Of these, the first is not possible, because the non-apprehension has been accepted as having the nature of apprehension of something else, and because its own nature is directly realized through the perception of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana-pratyakṣa</s>) — whence is there room for the fault of essential unestablishedness?

body.text: athocyate svasambedanameva na sambhavati / svātmani kriyāvirodhāt / na hi tayaivāsidhārayā saivāsidhārā cchidyate / tadebāṅgalyagraṃ tenaivāṅgulyagreṇa spṛśyate iti / ato 'sidva evāyaṃ hetuḥ / tadidaṃ svasambedanaśabdārthā parijñānavijṛmbhatameva prakaṭayati vāvaḥ / tathāhi kalasakaladhautakuvalayādibhyo vyāvṛttaṃ vijñānamupajāyate / tena bodharūpatayotpattirevāsya svasambittirucyate, prakāśavat / na karmmakarttṛkriyābhāvāt / ekasyānaṃśarūpasya trairūpyānupapattitaḥ / yathaiva hi prakāśakāntaranirapekṣaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśamāna ātmanaḥ prakāśaka ucyate / tathā jñānamapi jñānāntaranirapekṣaṃ prakāśamānamātmanaḥ prakāśamucyate / tato 'yaṃ paramārthaḥ / na jñānaṃ jñānāntarasaṃvedyamupapadyate nāpyasambiditamucyate / yathāprakāre ca svasambedanaśabdārtha vivakṣite na kiñcid vacanīyakamasti kuto yathoktadoṣāvasaraḥ / nāpi viśeṣaṇāsidvyāsidvirūdbhāvanīyā / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatayā sāmānyasya svayameva parairupagamāt / tathānabhyupagame vā na sāmānyabalena vā kuleyādiṣvanugatākārau dhīdhvanī syātāṃ / na hi yato yatra jñānābhidhānapravṛttistadanupalakṣaṇe tasya pratītirbhavati, daṇḍivat / yat punaridamudyotitamudyotakareṇa / kiṃ sāmānyaṃ pratipadyase, na vā / yadi pratipadyase kathamapanhuṣe / atha na pratipadyase tadā tasyāsidvatvādāśrayāsidvo hetuḥ / tadidaṃ tasya dharmmisvarūpitānabhijñatāvijṛmbhitamābhāti / yato na vayaṃ vahīrūpatayā sāmānyaṃ dharmmitayāṅgīkurmmahe / antarmmātrābhiniveśino bhāvābhāvobhayānubhavāhitavāsanāparipākaprabhavasyādhyastavahirvastuno jñānākārasya dharmbhitayopayogāt /
body.translated_text: Now it is said: self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) itself is not possible, because action upon oneself is contradictory. For that very sword-edge does not cut that same sword-edge; that very fingertip is not touched by that same fingertip. Therefore this reason is unestablished. This merely displays the manifestation of ignorance of the meaning of the word '<s>svasaṃvedana</s>' (self-awareness) on your part. For a cognition arises that is distinguished from pots, shards, washed garments, blue lotuses, and so forth. Therefore, its very arising in the form of awareness is called its self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>), like light — not because there is [a reflexive relation of] object, agent, and action, for a three-fold nature is impossible for what is unitary and without parts. For just as light, independent of another illuminator, shining forth, is called the illuminator of itself, so too cognition, independent of another cognition, shining forth, is called the illumination of itself. Therefore, this is the ultimate meaning: cognition cannot be cognized by another cognition, nor is it said to be un-cognized. And when the meaning of the word '<s>svasaṃvedana</s>' is intended in this manner, there is nothing to be objected to — whence is there opportunity for the stated fault? Nor should unestablishedness be raised through the unestablishedness of the qualifier, because the opponents themselves accept that the universal fulfills the conditions of apprehensibility (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>). Otherwise, if it were not accepted, then cognition and verbal expression following the common form upon well-bred [cows] and such would not occur through the force of the universal. For wherever there is the operation of cognition and designation arising from something, there is no cognition of that thing when it lacks the conditions of perceptibility, like a staff-bearer. Now, as for what has been illuminated by <s>Udyotakara</s>: 'Do you cognize the universal or not? If you cognize it, how do you deny it? If you do not cognize it, then since it is unestablished, the reason has an unestablished locus' — this appears to be merely a display of his ignorance of the nature of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). For we do not accept the universal as the property-bearer in the form of an external reality. Because what serves as the property-bearer is the cognitive image (<s>jñānākāra</s>) — which is solely internal in focus, which arises from the maturation of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) deposited by the experience of existence, non-existence, and both, and upon which the external object is superimposed.

body.text: sa ca svasambedanapratyakṣasidvatayā na śakyaḥ pratikṣeptuṃ / tadatra dharmmiṇi vyavasthitāḥ sadasatve cintayanti / kimayaṃ sāmānyaśabdavikalpapratibhāsārtho dharmmī paraparikalpitavahiḥsāmānyanibandhano veti / tasya vāhyānupādānatve sādhyatayānupalambho hetuḥ / na punastasyaivābhāvaḥ sādhyate / tadviṣayaśabdaprayogaprasaṅgāt / evambidhe ca dharmmiṇi vivakṣite kuta āśrayāsidvidoṣaḥ / yattūcyate / pratyakṣapramāṇasidvasvabhāvatayā sāmānyasyāsidva evāyaṃ heturiti / tadayuktaṃ, tasya svarūpeṇāpratibhāsanāt /
body.translated_text: And that [<s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer)] cannot be rejected, since it is established by the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) of self-awareness. Here, those who are established regarding the <s>dharmin</s> deliberate upon its existence or non-existence: 'Is this <s>dharmin</s> — the object appearing in the conceptual cognition associated with the word "<s>sāmānya</s> (universal)" — grounded in an external universal posited by others, or not?' When the external [universal] is not the material cause, non-apprehension is the logical reason, since it is what is to be proven. However, the very non-existence of that [universal] is not what is being proven, because of the absurdity that words referring to it would then be used. And when the <s>dharmin</s> is intended in this manner, whence arises the fault of unestablished locus? As for what is said — that this is an unestablished reason because the <s>sāmānya</s> is established as having a nature proven by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) — that is incorrect, because it does not appear in its own form.

body.text: idameva hi pratyakṣasya pratyakṣatvaṃ yat svarūpasya svabudvau samarpaṇaṃ / idaṃ punarmūlyādānakrayi sāmānyaṃ svarūpañca nādarśayati pratyakṣatāñca svīkarttumicchati / tathāhi na vayaṃ parasparāsaṃkīrṇaśāvaleyādivyaktibhedapratibhāsanavelāyāṃ tadvilakṣaṇamaparamanugatamadhyakṣeṇekṣāmahe / kaṇṭheśanamiva bhūteṣu / śāvaleyasāmānyabudverasidveḥ / tat kathamadṛṣṭakalpanayātmānamātmanā vipralabhemahi /
body.translated_text: For indeed, this is what constitutes the perceptual nature of perception: the presentation of its own form to one's own cognition. But this universal, like a buyer who takes the price but does not show the goods, neither reveals its own form nor does it wish to claim the status of being perceptible. For we, at the time when the distinct individual appearances of dogs and the like manifest without mutual confusion, do not perceive with direct perception anything different from them that persists across them — like a choking sensation among beings. Since the cognition of dog-universality is unestablished, how then could we deceive ourselves by imagining something unseen?

body.text: iti nāsidvo hetuḥ / nāpyanaikāntikatā śaṅkāviṣayamatipatati, vipakṣavṛttyadarśanāt / asapakṣe sambhavānupalambhāt / sādhāraṇānaikāntikatā mābhūta / sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatā tu pratibandhādarśanādanivārita prasaraiva /
body.translated_text: Thus the reason is not unestablished. Nor does the suspicion of inconclusiveness fall within the scope of doubt, because no occurrence in the dissimilar instance is observed; because of the non-apprehension of its possibility in the non-concordant instance. Let there be no common inconclusiveness. But the inconclusiveness of doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar instance, due to the non-observation of invariable concomitance, has indeed unrestricted scope.

body.text:
tadetanna samālocitatarkakarkaśadhiyāmabhidhānaṃ / viparyyaye bādhakapramāṇasāmarthyādapasāritasadbhāvatvāttadāśaṅkāyāḥ / tathāhyasattve sādhye sattvaṃ vipakṣaḥ / tatra pratyakṣavṛttyā bhavitavyaṃ / yato yadyadāvikalāpratihatasāmarthyaṃ tattadā bhavatyeva / tadyathāvikalabalasakalakāraṇakalāpo 'ṅkuraḥ / sati ca cakṣurādisākalye dṛśye vastunyavikalāpratibadvaśaktikāraṇaṃ pratyakṣaṃ jñānamiti svabhāvahetuḥ / tato virudvopalambhādvipakṣādvyāvarttamāno hetuḥ / asadvyavahārayogyatvena vyāpyata iti vyāptisidvernānaikāntikaḥ / abhimatasādhya pratibandhasidvestu virudvatā dūratarasamutsāritarabhasaprasaraiva / ato 'sidvatādidūṣaṇaśaṅkākalaṅkālaṅki(kṛ)tādvetoḥ prastutavastusidvau sidvamasattvaṃ sāmānyasyetyalamatibadvavistaravisāriṇyā kathayeti viramyate /
na ca vastusaṃsthānavat sāmānyaṃ vyakterlakṣaṇaṃ / na cānuvṛttavyāvṛttavarṇādyātmake jātivyaktī varṇādiniyatapratibhāsapratītiprasaṅgāt / vyakterevāsau pratibhāsa iti cet ko 'parastarhi sāmānyasyānugatākāra iti cet /
body.translated_text:
This is not the statement of those whose intellects are hardened by well-considered reasoning. Because, through the power of a contradicting means of valid knowledge in the case of the opposite, the existence [of the universal] has been set aside, and therefore that suspicion is removed. For when non-existence is what is to be proven, existence is the dissimilar instance. There, occurrence through perception must obtain. Because whatever has its capacity unimpaired and unobstructed at a given time, that necessarily comes into being at that time — just as a sprout arises when the complete aggregate of causes has its full potency. And when the sense faculties such as the eye are complete and the object is visible, perceptual cognition is a cause whose power is unimpaired and unobstructed — this is the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (natural reason). Therefore, the reason, turning away from the dissimilar instance through <s>viruddhopalambha</s> (contradictory perception), is pervaded by fitness for the convention of non-existence; hence the establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) ensures it is not inconclusive. As for the establishment of invariable concomitance with the intended object to be proven, the force of contradiction has been most thoroughly removed.
Therefore, from this reason — cleansed of the stain of suspicion regarding the faults of unestablishedness and the like — the non-existence of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is established for the matter at hand. Enough with this discourse that spreads into excessive elaboration — let us cease.
Nor is <s>sāmānya</s> the defining characteristic of a <s>vyakti</s> (particular), like material configuration. And if <s>jāti</s> (universal) and <s>vyakti</s> (particular) consist of recurring and distinguishing colors and the like, there would be the absurdity of cognition appearing as fixed in color and such attributes. If it is said that this appearance belongs to the <s>vyakti</s> alone — then what other entity is the recurring form of <s>sāmānya</s>?

body.text: nanu varṇasaṃsthāne virahayya kimaparamanugāmi vidyate / jātibyaktayoḥ samavāyabalādavibhāvitavibhāgayoḥ kṣīrodakayoriva parasparamiśraṇena pratipatteriti cet / na tarhi sāmānyaviśeṣayorekatarasyāpi rūpaṃ gṛhītaṃ / svarūpāgrahaṇe 'nayorapyagrahaṇamiti nirālambanaiva sā tādṛśī pratipattiriti paramārtha āveditastāvat nirālambanayā ca pratītyā vyavasthāpyamānaṃ sāmānyaṃ suvyavasthāpitaṃ / tasmādviśeṣyāsidvyāpi nāyamasidvo hetuḥ / sapakṣe varttamāno virudva ityapi na mantavyaḥ / anaikāntikatāpyasya na sambhāvanām arhati / asadvyavahārā napekṣatvena hi dṛśyānupalambho vyāptaḥ / yadi hi sannapi tatra na pravarttayet / iha sāpekṣaḥ syāt / tato vipakṣādvyāpakavirudvāvarudvāt / vyāvarttamāno 'sadvyavahāre viśrāmyatīti atastenāsadvyavahāreṇānupalambho vyāpyata iti kuto 'nekāntaḥ / tataśca sa evārthaḥ samāyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: Setting aside color and configuration, what else that is recurring exists? Since <s>jāti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>, whose distinction has not been discerned due to the force of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), are apprehended through mutual intermixture like milk and water — Reply: Then the form of neither the universal nor the particular has been grasped. When the own-form is not grasped, neither of these is grasped either — so such a cognition is entirely without a real basis. This is the ultimate truth that has been revealed. And a <s>sāmānya</s> established by a cognition that is without a real basis is well-established indeed [as non-existent]. Therefore, even through the unestablishedness of the qualificand, this reason is not unestablished. Nor should it be thought that it is contradictory because it occurs in the concordant instance. Its inconclusiveness too does not merit consideration. For non-apprehension of the visible is pervaded by fitness for the convention of non-existence. If, even when existing, it did not operate there, then it would be dependent here — and therefore, since the pervading contradictory is excluded from the dissimilar instance, the reason, turning away, rests in the convention of non-existence. Thus non-apprehension is pervaded by that convention of non-existence — whence then any inconclusiveness? And so the same conclusion has been reached.

children.translated_text: In these five fingers of perceptual cognition, clearly shining forth,

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhamihekṣate yaḥ śṛṅgaṃ śirasyātmana īkṣate saḥ //
children.translated_text: He who perceives a sixth thing — the universal (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) — here [among the five fingers], perceives a horn on his own head.

body.translated_text: And the ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>) of all that was stated before is this:

body.text: pratyakṣapratibhāsi vartmana pañcasvaṅgulīṣu sthitaṃ sāmānyaṃ pratibhāsate na ca vikalpākārabudvau tathā /
body.translated_text: In the path of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) appears as situated in the five fingers, but it does not appear in the same way in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpākārabuddhi</s>);

body.text: tā evāsphuṭamūrttayotra hi vibhāsante na jātistataḥ
body.translated_text: those very [fingers] with indistinct forms appear here, not the universal (<s>jāti</s>); therefore,
these two — single apprehension (<s>ekopalabdhi</s>) and linguistic convention (<s>dhvani</s>) — are rather the causes of the error of similarity (<s>sādṛśyabhrama</s>).
<s>Sāmānyasiddhidūṣaṇadikprasāritā</s> (Elaboration in the Direction of Refuting the Establishment of Universals), section 3.
